title: Mark docs/design/reviews/ athena-readonly in .gitattributes
summary: Add a `/docs/design/reviews/** athena-readonly` rule to .gitattributes so agents can read the review documents but no Athena job can change them. The audience is the repository owner, who wants rehearsal jobs unable to edit a review, for example to mark a finding fixed.

defaults_applied.how: Enforced by the git attribute that admission checks, not by prose.
A single-line rule in one file, plus a header comment if needed.
A criterion requires that the existing policy or admission tests still pass, and that a changed review file is rejected.
cargo test and clippy must stay green.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The existing `athena-readonly` attribute (decision D44, athena-v0.md §4.2) is the mechanism: it keeps files visible in snapshots and makes the admission check reject any change to them.
The `/src/**` pattern in the tests shows directory globs are supported, so one `/docs/design/reviews/**` line covers the 16 current files and any future ones.
Reviews are the owner's or reviewer's record, so a job that legitimately needs a new review is out of scope. New files under the path would also be blocked, which is accepted.
The edit to .gitattributes itself is permitted for this job because the request names it. The base's rules apply at landing, so this job is not blocked by its own rule.

acceptance_criteria.text: .gitattributes contains a rule marking everything under /docs/design/reviews/ (glob `/docs/design/reviews/**`) as `athena-readonly`. The existing /CLAUDE.md, /BRIEF.md and /LICENSE rules are unchanged.
The owner can see from the diff that only .gitattributes changed, with no edits to review text and nothing else in governance files.

`cargo test` passes, including the xtask policy test and the athena-git attrs tests, which classify paths by the committed .gitattributes at HEAD. Any file under docs/design/reviews/ is classified as readonly. Run `cargo test` to check.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or correcting the existing review documents or their findings.
Changing the admission logic or adding new attribute kinds.
Filesystem-level chmod or CI enforcement beyond the attribute.
departures: The change is a one-line attribute edit, so cost and time are lower than the reference. The main risks are an unsupported glob form and a policy test that enumerates readonly paths.
